newsitem.title: USA: PureTec initiates unit sale, restructure.
newsitem.headline: PureTec initiates unit sale, restructure.

text.p: PureTec Corp said on Monday that it had initiated the sale of its Styrex Industries subsidiary as part of a series of restructuring actions designed to improve future earnings.
The plastic products producer also said 10 percent of the employee base at its Burlington Resins subsidiary, or some 15 jobs, had been reduced as part of the plan.

The announcement accompanied the release of PureTec's earning results for the third quarter ended April 30, in which it posted net income from continuing operations of $2.3 million, or $0.08 per share, compared with $5.1 million, or $0.19 for the year-ago period.

The company noted that its gargen hose division had seen unfavorable weather conditions this year and that a recent industry-wide drop in Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) prices had also affected results.

PureTec said its restructuring actions included expanding its medical plastics capacity in the western United States and Europe, reducing workforce and overhead costs at the Burlington Resins subsidiary, initiating a sale of the Styrex Industries subsidiary and writing down most of its remaining investment in Evolutions Inc.
"Styrex has been reclassified as a discontinued operation effective with the third quarter of 1997, and 1996 results have been restated to reflect this change," the company said.
